name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
description: Holds US Treasury bills maturing within 3 months. Price barely moves; total return roughly tracks short-term interest rates. Works as a cash substitute.

name: Vanguard Intermediate-Term Treasury ETF
description: Holds US Treasury notes with 3-10 years to maturity. Moderate rate sensitivity: gains when rates fall, loses when they rise.

name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
description: Holds US Treasury bonds with 20+ years to maturity. The most rate-sensitive mainstream Treasury ETF — big moves in both directions when rates change.

name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
description: Holds ~10,000 US investment-grade bonds (Treasuries, corporates, mortgage-backed). One-ticket exposure to the whole US bond market.

name: iShares iBoxx USD Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF
description: Holds investment-grade corporate bonds. Yields more than Treasuries in exchange for credit risk; sells off when credit conditions worsen.

name: iShares iBoxx USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF
description: Holds below-investment-grade (junk) corporate bonds. Higher yield, but tends to fall alongside stocks in market stress.

name: iShares TIPS Bond ETF
description: Holds US Treasuries whose principal is indexed to CPI inflation. Hedges inflation surprises; still carries interest-rate risk.

name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
description: Holds the ~500 largest US companies (S&P 500). The default building block for US stock market exposure.

name: Invesco QQQ Trust
description: Holds the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies. Tech/growth heavy — historically higher return and volatility than SPY.

name: ProShares Ultra QQQ
description: Delivers 2x the DAILY return of the Nasdaq-100 via derivatives. Long-run result is path-dependent (volatility drag), not simply 2x.

name: ProShares UltraPro QQQ
description: Delivers 3x the DAILY return of the Nasdaq-100. Extreme drawdowns (over -75% in 2022); long-run return is path-dependent, not 3x.

name: Vanguard FTSE Developed Markets ETF
description: Holds thousands of developed-market stocks outside the US (Europe, Japan, etc.). Diversifies away from US-only exposure.

name: Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF
description: Holds ~100 US companies with 10+ consecutive years of dividends and strong balance sheets. Total return = price + dividends; tilts toward value sectors.

name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
description: Holds thousands of emerging-market stocks (China, India, Taiwan, Brazil). Higher growth potential with currency and political risk; tends to struggle when the US dollar is strong.

name: iShares Russell 2000 ETF
description: Holds ~2,000 US small-cap companies. More domestically focused and economically sensitive than large caps — swings harder in both directions.

name: Vanguard Real Estate ETF
description: Holds US real estate investment trusts (REITs) — companies owning offices, apartments, warehouses. Sensitive to interest rates and property cycles.

name: SPDR Gold Shares
description: Each share is backed by physical gold in vaults; tracks the gold price. No yield — often held as a crisis or inflation hedge.
